morph_technique:
THE CHANGE HAPPENS BEHIND SOMETHING. Danney, 2026-07-28: *"when Naruto does his clone technique there's a poof cloud out of nowhere to cover the part that is morphing — when the smoke goes away it's revealed the new identity."* That is the right mechanism and the reason is technical: a generator is poor at morphing a face and good at occluding one. Interpolating a human head into an animal's over a second and a half gives you mush; hiding the instant of change behind something gives you two easy halves and one clean reveal.

What it must NOT be is a puff of cartoon smoke. This film's register forbids anything novelty or comic, and its own edit forbids dissolve, wipe and whip pan — so the cover is never an effect. It is a REAL OBJECT ALREADY IN THE ROOM, moving through the frame in front of the head: steam, a garment, a bow arm, spray. Same structure as the poof, dressed as the film.

A man with a peacock's head stands at the centre of a long symmetrical walk-in closet. Over six seconds he surveys both walls, walks toward camera trailing one hand along the rail, lifts his hand away, then turns and walks off down the aisle. He touches everything and takes nothing.

@closet_man — adult male, slim, charcoal grey two-piece suit, white shirt, dark tie. His head is a peacock's: iridescent teal-and-green plumage, white eye-stripe, pale beak, thin crest of feathers upright on the crown. The head stays a peacock's in every single frame. 100% matches the reference.
@walk_in_closet — symmetrical rows of hanging garments both sides, neutral open rail, warm wood cabinetry, polished dark wood floor, arched doorway at the far end on the centreline. 100% matches the reference.
@yellow_object — one warm yellow #E7B93A sleeve hanging on the left rail at chest height, the only saturated colour in frame.

LOCATION MAP
Foreground: the aisle floor running to the bottom of frame. Midground: the man on the centreline. Background: the arched doorway, dead centre, warmly lit beyond. Rails and shelving recede symmetrically left and right. Camera sits low-centre in the aisle looking straight down it. Light comes from strip lighting under each shelf on both walls, plus a skylight panel overhead.

Frame one is already full: the man stands centred at mid-depth, shoulders square to camera, hands at his sides, peacock head facing straight down the lens. Perfect bilateral symmetry — the doorway arch centred behind his head. The yellow sleeve reads on the left rail.

FORMAT MODE
One continuous shot, the camera does not cut on its own.

OPTICS
WS at 63°, rectilinear, held at 63° for the full six seconds, no drift mid-shot. Shallow focus falls off past his shoulders; the rails soften into depth while he stays sharp.

CAMERA
Eye-level, centred on the aisle, operator anchored on the centreline. A slow continuous push-in at 1 km/h for the whole six seconds, straight in, same speed and direction throughout. Wide tonal latitude, soft highlight roll-off on the strip lights.

4.5s to 6.0s — he turns away from camera and walks down the aisle toward the arch at 3 km/h, receding, shoulders squaring smaller against the lit doorway, still walking as the shot ends.

Hanging garments swing on their hangers with real mass and settle within a beat of his passing. His footfalls land with weight on the hard polished floor. Contact shadow stays under him throughout.

Warm practical strip lighting under every shelf on both walls, 3200K, even and generous, plus a soft overhead skylight wash. Exposure sits bright and clean — an expensive, fully-lit room with no dark corners.

STYLE
Photoreal, glossy luxury-commercial, medium-high contrast, very fine grain, subtle bloom around the strip lights and the skylight.

OUTPUT SETTINGS
4K, 16:9, real time throughout.

The head remains a peacock's head for all six seconds. The frame stays bilaterally symmetrical with the arch on the centreline. The push-in runs unbroken at one constant speed. The warm yellow sleeve stays on the left rail and in frame. He walks away from camera at the end and is still walking when the shot ends. One man only in frame.
